subject: How to create linear combination of nested random components?

messages.author: 4b63675507b4aa11
messages.subject: How to create linear combination of nested random components?
parts:
Dear All,

My two-level disease mapping model has random effects at both the county-level and state-level (there are 3108 counties nested within 49 states):

> f <- out ~ 1 + f(county_id, model = "bym", graph = "nb.adj") + f(state_id, model = "iid")

I can easily create a linear combination of one random component and the intercept by:

> lcs1 <- inla.make.lincombs(county_id = diag(3108), "(Intercept)" = rep(1,3108))
> lcs2 <- inla.make.lincombs(state_id = diag(49), "(Intercept)" = rep(1,49))

But how can I create a linear combination of the two random components? I tried:

> lcs3 <- inla.make.lincombs(county_id = diag(3108), state_id = diag(49))

But it apparently did not work.

Many thanks.

Best,
Shige

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to create linear combination of nested random components?
parts:
On Wed, 2017-08-23 at 03:49 -0700, Shige Song wrote:
>
> > lcs3 <- inla.make.lincombs(county_id = diag(3108), state_id =
> diag(49))

if 'x' id country_id and 'y' is state_id, then linear combinations of
these are

Ax + By


so you need nrow(A) = nrow(B), which is not the case for you.


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to create linear combination of nested random components?
parts:
No. My goal is to obtain marginal posterior distribution of the sum of the two random components (i.e., county_id and state_id). I am following examples (p. 159-161) in Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA.

Best,
Shige

On Wed, 2017-08-23 at 04:23 -0700, Shige Song wrote:
> No. My goal is to obtain marginal posterior distribution of the sum
> of the two random components (i.e., county_id and state_id). I am
> following examples (p. 159-161) in Spatial and Spatio-Temporal
> Bayesian Models with R-INLA.

yes, but this is not what you write.

if x has length 1, and y length two, and you want the sums, its


x[1] + y[1]

and

x[1] + y[2]


so its

inla.make.lincombs(x = matrix(1,1,2), y = diag(2))
